Question Choices: Select the correct name for this angle: ~~<XYZ | <ZXY | <ZYB | <XYB~~
Hints: The vertex must be the middle letter. The first and last letters lie on the two marked rays.
Solution: The marked angle has vertex Y and arms YX and YB, so its name is angle XYB (or BYX). XYZ and ZYB use YZ; ZXY has vertex X.

Question Choices: Select the correct name for this angle: ~~<SOP | <POQ | <SOQ~~
Hints: The vertex must be the middle letter. The first and last letters lie on the two marked rays.
Solution: The green arc starts on OP and ends on OQ; O is the vertex. Angle POQ uses those arms. SOP and SOQ use OS and do not cover the full marked opening.

Question Choices: Select which angle measure is greater?: ~~<XYB | <ZAC~~
Hints: Compare the openings between the rays, not the lengths of the drawn arms.
Solution: Angle XYB opens wider than a right angle. Angle ZAC is acute, so angle XYB is greater. Compare openings, not drawn arm lengths.

Question Choices: Select which angle measure is smaller?: ~~<PQS | <TQR~~
Hints: Compare the openings between the rays, not the lengths of the drawn arms.
Solution: Angle PQS is the smaller acute opening. Angle TQR is obtuse, so angle PQS has the smaller measure.

Question Choices: Select what type of angle is shown in the image: ~~Acute | Obtuse | Right~~
Hints: Compare with 90 degrees and 180 degrees: acute below 90, right 90, obtuse between 90 and 180, straight 180.
Solution: The marked opening is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees, so it is obtuse, not acute or right.
